hook
One tiny pellet of uranium, about the size of your fingertip, holds as much energy as a ton of coal. How do we unlock it?
fission
It starts with an atom. A tiny particle called a neutron hits a uranium atom, and the atom splits in two.
fission
This is called fission. It releases a burst of heat, and two or three new neutrons fly out.
chain
Those neutrons hit more atoms, which split and release even more neutrons. This is a chain reaction.
control
To keep it safe and steady, control rods soak up spare neutrons. Push them in to slow the reaction down, pull them out to speed it up.
reactor
All of this happens inside the reactor core, in long fuel rods, surrounded by water.
heat
The heat from fission makes the water super hot. It's kept under high pressure, so it doesn't boil.
steam
That hot water flows to a steam generator, where it boils a separate loop of water into steam.
turbine
The steam blasts through a turbine, spinning it at high speed. The turbine turns a generator, and that makes electricity.
cooling
Then the steam is cooled back into water, using giant cooling towers. That white cloud is just water vapour, not smoke.
green
A nuclear plant releases almost no carbon dioxide, and can power around a million homes, day and night.
outro
Splitting atoms to light up cities. Follow for more science made simple!
